changes: packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-registry.ts: added the ten ProofStory intent-hardening artifact filenames (original-intent-snapshot, milestone-ledger, milestone-closeout, slice-plan, parent-ledger-rollup, proofstory, intent-collision, scope-shrinkage-decision, red-evidence, spike .json) to LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES, the closed set consulted by classifyLifecycleArtifact — so the scope gate now classifies these command-generated story metadata files as lifecycle_artifact pass instead of out_of_scope fail. packages/main/src/tasks/scope-contract-smoke.ts: new proofStoryPositive block pins all ten as scope.lifecycle_artifact:B-scope:<name> pass rows under an enforce contract that lists no story-metadata paths; per-row assertions run before the aggregate status check (F-001) so a regression names the exact artifact.
usage: No new command surface. Owners of high-assurance stories simply run the existing flow — lattice scope_contract_check / story_advance — and the ProofStory artifacts their commands generate (original_intent_snapshot_set, intent_collision_set, red_evidence_create, proofstory_contract_set, milestone_ledger_set, spike_start, ...) no longer block the DEV->REVIEW scope gate or need scope_contract_acknowledge. Regression check: node packages/main/dist/tasks/scope-contract-smoke.js
expectedOutcome: Under a mode=enforce scope contract that does not list story-metadata paths, all ten ProofStory artifact paths under .lattice/story/actives/<id>/ produce scope.lifecycle_artifact pass rows (blocking=false) in scope_contract_check, exactly like checklist.json; unknown filenames still fail closed.
actualTranscript: Pre-fix baseline (RED-001): classifier probe printed 'RED: not lifecycle_artifact -> <all ten names>' exit 1. Post-fix: same probe prints 'GREEN: all ten lifecycle_artifact' exit 0; scope-contract smoke prints 'scope contract smoke passed'; this story's own scope_contract_check ran status=pass with its ProofStory artifacts classified as lifecycle rows (self-demonstrating). Bite test: removing proofstory.json from the compiled registry fails the smoke with 'B-12a1 ProofStory lifecycle row proofstory.json: expected scope row not found'.
outcomeDiff: No difference — expected and actual match on all ten names, the negative fail-closed cases, and the self-demonstrating story run.
limitations: Deliberate carve-outs: grill.json, clusters.json (registry still lists stale singular cluster.json) and scope-extension-decisions.json are different command families, tracked as a follow-up story already started by the user; process-fact registry misses milestone-closeout.json (separate follow-up chip). Forward-only fix: B-623a's hand-added acknowledgements are not retroactively cleaned. Acceptance proven at checkScopeContract/smoke level (same code path as the live gate), no end-to-end replay of a full high-assurance story.
pitfalls: 1) The story about ProofStory artifacts itself triggered the ProofStory high-assurance gate (gate wording) — it had to produce the very artifacts it registers; the fixed classifier then let its own metadata pass, self-validating. 2) Candidate milestone ledger must be re-confirmed via intent_collision_set pass AFTER milestone_ledger_set, else missing_confirmed_milestone_ledger blocks DEV. 3) An honest codex FAIL (F-001, aggregate-only smoke diagnostic) mid-REVIEW forces the full DEV->REVIEW round restart + evidence refresh + all-lane re-review — commit finding fixes knowing the cascade cost. 4) Concurrent dist bite-tests by parallel reviewers on the shared worktree can race; serialize destructive dist experiments or use an isolated worktree copy. 5) scope_contract_init_from_plan produced empty allowed sets; declare paths explicitly with scope_contract_set.
